title: First post here: a month of building an idle factory game with generative AI (code, 3D, art, animation
author: ManduLaboratory
selftext:
This video is short and only has brief information. It shows a small part of the game and isn't a full gameplay walkthrough. There's no Steam page yet (I'm still setting up my Steamworks account), so there's nothing to wishlist yet, and I don't have a release date or price.

Hi everyone, this is my first post on Reddit, so please be gentle if I get the etiquette wrong. I'm a solo developer (mandu laboratory), and I'm posting here because almost all of my game is built with generative AI, and I'd like to compare notes with people doing the same. English isn't my first language and I use a translator to write this, so please forgive any awkward wording.

The game, briefly:

It's called Factoridle: Welcome, Administrator, an idle factory game for PC with a story-driven narrative at its center. It's inspired by Factorio. I love that game, but it eats a huge amount of time that I don't have, so I decided to make the idle, auto-building version I wanted to play myself. You don't place buildings. You act as the Administrator and only set priorities, research and upgrades. The factory finds its own bottlenecks, turns them into construction jobs, and drones build them. The story is the other half of the game: you play a sleepy Administrator who approves a new outpost, and as the factory grows, dialogue, emails from a company and event CG slowly start to feel strange. I'll leave the rest unspoiled. It's been in development for a little over a month.

How I used AI:

I wrote the code with Claude Code (Sonnet, Opus and Fable models), and a second agent reviewed the designs and code.

For 3D, I used Meshy (nano-banana-pro for concepts, meshy-7.1 for image-to-3D) and cleaned the results up in Blender. For modular pieces like belts, I used Blender scripts instead (also written with Claude's help).

The character art comes from GPT image generation through the Codex CLI. Style drift was the hardest problem, and one fixed reference image per request fixed most of it.

I also used MiniMax H3, running locally in ComfyUI, to animate the in-game character portraits and to turn the event CG into short videos, then converted the clips into PNG sequences for the game.

I didn't use generative models for music or sound effects. They are synthesized with scripts that Claude helped me write.

What worked: turning rough designs into working systems quickly, and having a second agent review the code.

What didn't: keeping one art style across generated images, and anything that needs exact geometry or balance tuning, where I had to measure real results myself.

How do you keep an art style consistent across many generated images? And for those with big AI-written codebases, how do you catch the subtle bugs?

Thanks for reading, and I'm happy to go into more detail on any part of the workflow. I'm new here, so I'd really appreciate your advice and feedback. I plan to be around this community often, to read your posts and join the discussions, so I hope to learn a lot from you. Thank you!
